summary: 2 HIGH issues, 1 WARNING — all connections are real. The create-payment-intent edge function has a silent price default vulnerability, and a leftover Next.js env file creates a naming-confusion risk.

issues.issue: VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are read but not validated at startup — a missing env var only surfaces when an edge function call is attempted.
issues.fix: Consider adding an early validation check in apiService.ts or a startup guard in App.tsx that throws if these are missing.

issues.issue: STRIPE_PRICE_PRO and STRIPE_PRICE_ELITE env vars default to '99' and '199' respectively if missing. This means a misconfigured deployment could silently undercharge users (treating Elite as 199 THB instead of failing).
issues.fix: Use ?? instead of || so missing env vars produce NaN and fail the amount check. Or throw early like stripe-webhook/index.ts does.

critical_issues.issue: STRIPE_PRICE_PRO/ELITE default to string '99'/'199' via || operator instead of failing on missing env. If env vars are not set, prices silently default to these values instead of throwing an error.
critical_issues.fix: Replace `parseInt(Deno.env.get('STRIPE_PRICE_PRO') ?? '99')` with a strict guard that throws if the env var is missing. Example: `const price = Deno.env.get('STRIPE_PRICE_PRO'); if (!price) throw new Error('STRIPE_PRICE_PRO is not set'); parseInt(price)`. This matches the pattern already used correctly in stripe-webhook/index.ts lines 18-24.

critical_issues.issue: Root .env.local uses NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (Next.js convention) pointing to a different Supabase project (xyzcompany.supabase.co). The app/.env.local uses VITE_ prefix pointing to the correct project (pexcvfhuvqrwrabpgkzi.supabase.co). Vite does NOT read root .env.local, so this is not a runtime issue, but it indicates confusion from a potential Next.js → Vite migration. Leftover root .env.local should be removed or renamed to .env.local.bak to avoid future confusion.
critical_issues.fix: Delete or rename root .env.local. Vite only reads app/.env.local which is correctly configured.

critical_issues.issue: VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are used without startup validation — missing env vars only surface when the first edge function is called, producing a confusing runtime error.
critical_issues.fix: Add an early validation at module load time, similar to supabaseClient.ts: `if (!SUPABASE_URL || !ANON_KEY) throw new Error('[apiService] Missing VITE_SUPABASE_URL or VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY');`

warnings.issue: P1-01 MVP Decision: Email confirmation bypassed for faster onboarding. Users can sign up and access the app without verifying their email address. Supabase still sends the confirmation email in the background.
warnings.recommendation: Re-enable email confirmation before production launch. The auto-confirm pattern is a security tradeoff appropriate only for MVP.

warnings.issue: VITE_APP_URL defaults to localhost in both .env.example files. This variable is used for auth redirect URLs (AuthPage.tsx line 483: `${window.location.origin}/auth/callback`). On Vercel, window.location.origin is set automatically, so this default is harmless — but if it's used as a fallback and Vercel doesn't set it, redirects go to localhost.
warnings.fix: Verify Vercel sets VITE_APP_URL or VERCEL_URL in production environment, or remove the fallback and rely solely on window.location.origin.
